props.title: It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World
props.initialSlug: Epic chase for buried fortune drives strangers mad

sections.content: It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World revolutionized the big-budget comedy ensemble, throwing together comedy legends Milton Berle, Sid Caesar, Ethel Merman, and Mickey Rooney in a frenzied cross-country treasure hunt. Director Stanley Kramer, known for serious dramas like Judgment at Nuremberg (1961), went all-in on slapstick spectacle with elaborate car chases, airplane stunts, and physical comedy set pieces. The film's massive success inspired later star-studded chase comedies like The Great Race (1965) and Those Daring Young Men in Their Jaunty Jalopies (1969).

sections.content: The 1960s marked peak ensemble comedy, with The Russians Are Coming, The Russians Are Coming (1966) and What's New Pussycat? (1965) packing in maximum star power. These films balanced multiple storylines and gave each celebrity their moment to shine. The format influenced later classics like Airplane! (1980) and The Cannonball Run (1981), which maintained the manic energy while adding contemporary comedy stars. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

Modern directors still reference Kramer's epic comedy style. Rat Race (2001) directly homaged the premise with an ensemble including John Cleese, Whoopi Goldberg and Rowan Atkinson. Midnight Run (1988) and Due Date (2010) kept the cross-country chase format while focusing on smaller casts. The film's influence extends to animated features like Cars (2006), which captures similar road trip energy and southwestern landscapes.
